description: Suite of VNC servers and clients based on the VNC 4 branch of TightVNC
info:
1. Set a VNC password. It's stored in ~/.config/tigervnc/passwd:
vncpasswd

2. Choose the session and resolution in ~/.config/tigervnc/config. session is a desktop file's name from /usr/share/xsessions:
mkdir -p ~/.config/tigervnc
cat > ~/.config/tigervnc/config <<'EOF'
session=icewm-session
geometry=1920x1080
localhost
EOF
localhost makes the server accept connections only from the server itself and you reach it through an SSH tunnel (step 5). 
VNC password authentication is weak, so that's the safer default. 
Drop the line if you want to connect directly on your LAN.

3. Give display :1 to your user:
echo ':1=user' | sudo tee -a /etc/tigervnc/vncserver.users

4. Start it, and have it start at boot:
sudo systemctl enable --now vncserver@:1
systemctl status vncserver@:1
Display :1 listens on port 5901. If it doesn't stay up, check journalctl -u vncserver@:1 and the session log in ~/.local/state/tigervnc/.

5. Connect from your PC. With localhost set, tunnel through SSH:
ssh -L 5901:localhost:5901 serverip     # keep this open
vncviewer localhost:1
Without localhost, connect directly with vncviewer serverip:1.
